sources.title: Giant Wild Goose Pagoda in Xi'an: How to Visit (by a Local Guide)
sources.content:
Giant Wild Goose Pagoda - Complete Information

Basic Facts
The Giant Wild Goose Pagoda (also called Big Wild Goose Pagoda or Dayan Pagoda) is a significant Buddhist structure in southern Xi'an, China. Built in 652 during the Tang Dynasty, it was constructed to house Buddhist scriptures and statues brought back from India by the monk Xuanzang. The pagoda underwent reconstruction in 704 and received exterior renovations during the Ming Dynasty.

Key Statistics:
Height: 64.517 meters across 7 stories
Base length: 25.5 meters
Architectural style: Pavilion-style brick pagoda
Status: Tang Dynasty's largest and earliest square pavilion-style brick pagoda; UNESCO World Heritage site

Visiting Information
Hours: 8:30 AM - 5:00 PM
Admission: 30 CNY (approximately $4 USD)
Tower climbing: Additional 25 yuan ($3-4 USD)
No advance reservation required
Recommended Duration: 1-1.5 hours
Location: No. 1 Ci'en Road, Yanta District; approximately 20 minutes from city center

What to See Inside
Each floor contains distinct features:
First Floor: Inscribed tablets with names of imperial examination graduates
Second Floor: Sakyamuni Buddha statue
Third Floor: Birch bark scriptures from Xuanzang
Fourth Floor: Important religious relics
Fifth Floor: Tang Dynasty lotus-patterned bricks and wind chimes
Sixth-Seventh Floors: Observation decks with views of fountains and nearby structures

The pagoda contains "256 wooden staircase steps" requiring approximately 20 minutes to climb.

Giant vs. Small Wild Goose Pagoda
The Giant version is climbable and features "straight lines that make it look tall and sturdy," while the smaller pagoda displays "a slightly curved shape that gives it a more graceful feel." The Small pagoda stands at 43.4 meters (originally 15 stories, now 13 remaining).

Surrounding Attractions
Da Ci'en Temple complex with historic buildings
Great Hall of Buddha
Bell and Drum Towers
Temple gardens reflecting Tang Dynasty design
Pagoda forest with stone tablets from Tang through Qing dynasties
Grand Tang Dynasty Ever Bright City (evening performances)
Joy City (shopping and dining)

Best Times to Visit
Spring (April-May) and late autumn (November)
Morning visits (8:30-9:00 AM): Potential to hear monks reciting sutras
Afternoon (4:00-4:30 PM): Fewer crowds

Photography Tips
Xuanzang Master Statue foreground
Grand Tang Dynasty Ever Bright City northeast entrance
South Square of Joy City (using telephoto lens compression)
Southwest Peony Garden corner

Transportation
Line 3 subway to Big Wild Goose Pagoda Station; Exit C is approximately 985 meters (0.6 miles) from the pagoda

sources.title: Big Wild Goose Pagoda & Daci'en Temple Travel Guide 2026: History & Culture
sources.content:
Big Wild Goose Pagoda & Daci'en Temple - Complete Text Extract

Introduction & Overview
The Big Wild Goose Pagoda, also known as the "Daci'en Temple Pagoda," was constructed in 652 AD during the Tang Dynasty. It was built under the supervision of the legendary monk Xuanzang to house Buddhist scriptures and relics he brought back from India via the Silk Road. Initially designed as a five-story structure, the pagoda was reconstructed and now stands as a seven-story marvel, reaching 64.517 meters (211.5 feet) high with a base length of 25.5 meters (83.6 feet).

The pagoda exemplifies the fusion of traditional Chinese and ancient Indian architectural styles. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and part of the "Silk Roads: the Routes Network of Chang'an-Tianshan Corridor."

Location: Inside Daci'en Temple, Yanta District, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province

Operating Hours & Access
October 15 – February 28: 8:00 AM – 5:40 PM (last entry 4:40 PM)
March 1 – October 14: 8:30 AM – 6:00 PM (last entry 5:00 PM)

Musical Fountain Times:
12:00–12:10 PM
4:00–4:10 PM
7:00–7:10 PM
9:00–9:10 PM

Suggested Visiting Duration: 2–3 hours

Historical Background
Xuanzang traveled to India between 629 and 645 AD to study Buddhist teachings and returned with 657 volumes of sacred texts and numerous statues. The pagoda was constructed to preserve and honor these treasures.

The name "Big Wild Goose Pagoda" originates from Buddhist lore. According to legend, Xuanzang was guided to water by a flock of wild geese during his journey, saving his life.

Ticket Information
Daci'en Temple Admission:
Adults: 40 RMB (peak season), 30 RMB (off-season)
Children/Students: 20 RMB (peak season), 15 RMB (off-season) - for ages 6–18 and university undergraduates
Free Entry: Children under 6 or shorter than 1.2 meters; seniors 65 and above

Big Wild Goose Pagoda Climbing:
Adults: 25 RMB (peak season), 20 RMB (off-season)

Main Attractions
Daci'en Temple: One of the most significant Buddhist temples in Chinese history, originally built by Emperor Gaozong of the Tang Dynasty to honor his mother.
Big Wild Goose Pagoda: The seven-story pagoda stands as the defining landmark.
Xuanzang Sanzang Courtyard: Dedicated to the legacy of Xuanzang.
North Square Musical Fountain: One of the world's largest water fountain displays, free performances.
Grand Tang Dynasty Ever Bright City: A pedestrian street with Tang Dynasty cultural theme, free to explore.

Recommended Tour Route:
1. North Square - Begin at North Square to watch the musical fountain show
2. Ancient Poetry Street - Walk south to this cultural display
3. Xuanzang Statue - Visit this commemorative statue
4. Grand Tang Dynasty Ever Bright City (North Entrance)
5. Kaiyuan Square

Photography Spots:
Tang Daci'en Temple Ruins Park (South Gate)
Xuanzang Statue at Daci'en Temple Entrance
Dayuecheng Mall, Gate 3 - Red walls create unique visual effects
Dayuecheng Mall, 4th Floor Viewing Platform

Religious Ceremonies
Daci'en Temple regularly hosts Buddhist ceremonies open to all visitors. During college and high school entrance exam seasons, the temple holds prayer ceremonies to bless students. On the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month, the temple distributes free Laba porridge.

Dining Near Big Wild Goose Pagoda
Run Shaanxi Cuisine – Yanta Chang'an Branch
Location: Within Grand Tang Dynasty Ever Bright City
Average Cost: Approximately 50 RMB per person

Transportation & Access
By Metro: Take Xi'an Metro Line 3 or Line 4 and alight at Big Wild Goose Pagoda Station.
By Bus: Bus routes 5, 21, and 22 stop at North Square Station.
By Taxi: From Xi'an city center, expect 20–30 minutes with fares typically ranging from 20–40 RMB.

Luggage Storage: Free luggage storage available at the Xi'an Citizen Service Center near Big Wild Goose Pagoda Metro Station Exit C, daily from 9:00 AM to 10:00 PM.

Published: January 2, 2026

sources.title: How to Visit Big Wild Goose Pagoda in Xi'an (Tips, Photos & Map)
sources.content:
How to Visit Big Wild Goose Pagoda in Xi'an

The Giant Wild Goose Pagoda was built in 652 during the Tang Dynasty (618-907) to store the Buddhist scriptures and statues that the great monk Xuanzang brought back from ancient India. It has been added to the World Heritage List.

For the best experience, visit in the morning (8:30 am-9 pm) or in the afternoon (4 pm-4:30 pm). In the morning, if you're lucky, you might catch monks reciting sutras in the temple.

Visit the Big Wild Goose Pagoda for a stunning view of Xi'an from above, and take a moment to admire the original Buddhist inscriptions written in Sanskrit. Within the Da Ci'en Temple, you can explore historic buildings such as the Great Hall of Buddha, the Bell Tower, and the Drum Tower.

Visitors must absolutely stay until mid-afternoon or evening for the famous (and FREE!) fountain show that occurs all-year round, just outside the inner walls. It is Asia's largest water show, and is synchronized to a one-hour orchestral performance. It is a particularly spectacular show at night, due to the multicolored lights that accompany the show.

Allow at least 2-3 hours to fully explore the temple grounds and climb the pagoda.

Entry fee for Daci'en Temple is RMB 50, and ascending the Big Wild Goose Pagoda is an additional RMB 30. Summer hours (March 16 – December 4) are 08:00~17:30, and winter hours (December 04 – March 15) are 08:00~17:00.

You can take the subway to Big Wild Goose Pagoda Station on Line 3 and exit at Exit C, which is approximately 985 meters to the pagoda.

Luggage storage is available for free at the Xi'an Citizen Service Center, conveniently located near Big Wild Goose Pagoda Metro Station Exit C, operating daily from 9:00 AM to 10:00 PM.

sources.title: Giant Wild Goose Pagoda - Wikipedia
sources.content:
Giant Wild Goose Pagoda - Wikipedia

The Giant Wild Goose Pagoda, also known as the Big Wild Goose Pagoda, is a monumental Buddhist pagoda located in southern Xi'an and has been added to the World Heritage List. It was built in 652 during the Tang Dynasty (618-907) to store the Buddhist scriptures and statues that the great monk Xuanzang brought back from ancient India.

The pagoda was originally five stories and built with rammed earth before being rebuilt with bricks. It was extended to seven stories and renovated externally during the Ming Dynasty. The current pagoda stands at 64.517 meters tall with a base length of 25.5 meters.

Xuanzang, the monk for whom the pagoda was built, traveled to India to study and translate Sanskrit scriptures and developed influential Buddhist theories on consciousness, karma, and rebirth. The Tang government commissioned the structure specifically to encourage his leadership of the temple and facilitate Buddhist text translation and study.

The pagoda has sustained damage from weather, warfare, and earthquakes over centuries but remains a prominent architectural achievement. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Silk Roads network in 2014.

sources.content:
Giant Wild Goose Pagoda - TravelChinaGuide

The North Square's free musical fountain show is a must-do, with the fountain dancing in twenty-two patterns in perfectly choreographed movement—it's the largest musical fountain in Asia.

Through the windows on the upper floors, you'll see the peony garden to the west, the music fountain on the north square, and if weather is clear enough, the distant Qinling Mountains are also visible.

The temple complex spans 12.5 acres and takes some time to walk around, so good shoes are a must.

It is suggested to go to the north square in advance if you want to appreciate the night view of the music fountain, since there may be many people.

sources.title: 大雁塔（世界文化遗产、第一批全国重点文物保护单位）_百度百科
sources.content:
大雁塔文本内容提取

基本信息
大雁塔位于陕西省西安市雁塔区大慈恩寺内，是一座砖仿木结构的四方形楼阁式塔。该塔通高64.517米，底层边长25.5米，由塔基、塔身、塔刹三部分组成。

历史沿革

建造背景
唐永徽三年（652年），玄奘法师为保存从天竺经丝绸之路带回的经卷、佛像与舍利，主持修建了大雁塔。最初为五层结构，武则天长安年间（701-704年）改建为七层。明万历三十二年（1604年）进行了重大维修加固。

名称由来
塔名源于玄奘在印度所闻的传说。古印度摩揭陀国的僧人曾埋葬坠雁并建灵塔。玄奘仿照印度雁塔形式建造，故沿袭原名，前加"大"字以代表大乘佛教。

建筑特征
底层四面皆有石门。底层南门洞两侧镶嵌著名书法家褚遂良所书、唐太宗李世民撰文的《大唐三藏圣教序》和唐高宗李治撰文的《大唐三藏圣教序记》两通石碑，人称"二圣三绝碑"。

文物遗存

舍利
原存舍利数万余粒。1998年6月，印度玄奘寺住持释悟谦法师赠予两颗珍贵佛舍利。

贝叶经
四层塔室内供奉长约40厘米、宽约7厘米的贝叶经，刻有梵文，全球认识该文字的学者不足10位。

文化价值
大雁塔是现存最早、规模最大的唐代四方楼阁式砖塔，代表佛塔这种古印度建筑形式随佛教传入中原并融入华夏文化的过程。作为丝绸之路鼎盛时期的重要见证，该塔凝聚了中古劳动人民的智慧结晶。

雁塔文化

雁塔诗会
唐代众多诗人登临大雁塔赋诗作文。天宝十一年（752年）秋，杜甫与岑参、高适、薛据、储光羲相约登塔，各赋五言长诗一首，流传千古。

雁塔题名
新科进士登塔题名成为传统，象征步步高升。白居易27岁及第，题诗"慈恩塔下题名处，十七人中最少年"。明代举人亦效仿此习俗。

保护与遗产地位
1961年3月4日，国务院公布大雁塔为第一批全国重点文物保护单位。2014年6月22日，作为中国、哈萨克斯坦和吉尔吉斯斯坦联合申遗的"丝绸之路：长安-天山廊道的路网"中的遗址点，成功列入世界遗产名录。

旅游信息
地址：陕西省西安市雁塔区大雁塔街道广场东路3号
开放时间：09:00—17:00
门票价格：25元/人（淡季20元/人）
可乘坐地铁3、4号线至大雁塔站，或乘多条公交线路到达。

sources.title: 西安大雁塔游玩攻略 - 携程攻略
sources.content:
大雁塔游玩攻略

门票价格
大慈恩寺门票为50元/人（包含大雁塔登塔），或者根据另一信息源，大慈恩寺门票50元/人，登塔额外收费30元/人。

开放时间
开放时间为08:00-17:00，大雁塔登塔时间为09:00-18:00。

免票优惠政策
免票人群包括65周岁以上老年人、6周岁以下或身高1.2米以下儿童、现役军人、残疾人等凭有效证件免票。

主要游玩区域

大慈恩寺和大雁塔
大慈恩寺是唐代著名的佛教寺院，也是玄奘法师翻译佛经的地方，寺内建筑宏伟，佛像庄严。

北广场
大雁塔北广场是亚洲最大的喷泉广场和水景广场，占地252亩，由水景喷泉、文化广场、园林景观等构成。

南广场
大雁塔南广场建在大慈恩寺前面，广场上的标志性建筑是玄奘站立雕像，周围有园林绿地、花岗岩铺地和水面过桥等设施。

免费广场
雁塔广场全天免费开放，大慈恩寺围墙外的四个免费广场也可用于拍照合影。

How to Visit Big Wild Goose Pagoda in Xi'an: A Practical Guide

Summer hours (March 16 – December 4) are 08:00~17:30, and winter hours (December 04 – March 15) are 08:00~17:00.

You can take the subway to Big Wild Goose Pagoda Station on Line 3 and exit at Exit C, which is approximately 985 meters to the pagoda.

The North Square's free musical fountain show is a must-do. The temple complex spans 12.5 acres and takes some time to walk around, so good shoes are a must.
